summary: Outbound email spoof + automated service-account provisioning attempt observed after HR onboarding email spoof
description:
Issue summary:
A spike in outbound emails with forged 'From' headers (display name: 'People Ops <hr@redwood-internal.com>') was detected on 2026-03-10 14:22:13 UTC originating from our outbound-relay cluster. Shortly after the spike, an automated provisioning job attempted to create a new service account and attach a high-privilege role via IaC pipeline (observed in CI job infra-provision-42).

Impact:
- Potential exfil or lateral movement vector: attacker may be using spoofed HR emails to trick staff into clicking a malicious link or to validate active accounts.
- One IaC pipeline executed an unexpected provisioning action that attempted to create service-account 'onboard-bot-probe' and bind 'roles/editor' in project redwood-prod-us-east. The provisioning was rejected by policy but triggered audit alerts.

Environment:
- prod (us-east-1)
- Outbound-relay cluster: outbound-eu1 and outbound-us1 showed highest rates

Evidence / Logs:
- Mail headers and sample message stored in S3: s3://redwood-security/evidence/2026-03-10/spoofed-hr-email-142213.eml
- SIEM alert: SIEM#A-20260310-734 (severity high)
- Cloud audit log entry (IAM): projects/redwood-prod-us-east/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity at 2026-03-10T14:25:02Z (see commit abc1234 for referenced job)
- CI job: infra-provision-42 (build URL in comment)
- Observed source IPs for SMTP traffic: 35.216.14.22, 13.224.55.101 (geo: unknown / ASN suspicious), UA strings: Postfix/3.6.3 and custom-http-client/1.2.

Steps to reproduce / how issue was detected:
1) Automated outbound-relay anomaly detector (ruleset v2.4) flagged high ratio of mismatched SPF/DKIM for hr@redwood-internal.com on 2026-03-10 14:22 UTC.
2) SOC analyst (J. Rivera) pulled email samples and found redirect links pointing to a short-lived ngrok endpoint and a base64-encoded parameter.
3) Correlation with CI/CD logs showed an infra job executed shortly after an identifiable clicked link from a test user.

Investigation notes (initial):
- The email 'From' used display name matching People Ops but originated from third-party IPs; SPF failed, DKIM absent.
- No initial signs that our internal HR mailbox was compromised; mailbox logs show no outbound message at that time.
- The IaC pipeline run was triggered by a GitHub webhook from user 'dependabot[bot]' but with unusual commit metadata; GitHub audit log shows a PR merge from forked repo at 14:24:10Z (reviewed as suspicious).
- Policy enforcement prevented service-account key creation; the request was logged and automatically denied by org policy (org-policy-iam-privilege-binding).
- A single user (engineering-staging@redwood.com) clicked the link in a test environment; that account is flagged for follow-up but multi-factor remained in place and no credential changes were recorded.

Hypotheses:
- Attack vector likely external spoofing + social engineering to induce a CI action that triggers provisioning in infra.
- Possible chained compromise: attacker used valid webhook token or abused a forked repo PR to cause CI to run with elevated creds.

Actions taken so far:
- Blocked outbound SMTP connections from source IPs at the firewall and added to blocklist.
- Rotated CI service tokens for infra-provision pipeline and revoked recently issued webhook secrets.
- Temporarily disabled automatic merges from forks and added stricter branch protection rules.
- Created SOC watch rule to escalate any new outbound email SPF/DKIM failures for redwood-internal.com to P0.
- Opened a GitHub audit ticket and requested full audit for the infra repo (see related_github_prs).

Open questions / follow-ups needed:
- Identify whether any service account keys were exfiltrated earlier in the week (search window 2026-03-03 to 2026-03-10).
- Validate CI runner image integrity and recent maintainer ACL changes.
- Interview the user who clicked the link to understand the context and collect their browser artifacts.

Suggested remediation sequence (short-term):
1) Continue token rotation for CI and webhook secrets across infra-critical pipelines.
2) Force password reset + MFA re-check for any users who interacted with the suspicious email in prod.
3) Enforce DKIM for redwood-internal.com and tighten outbound relay SPF to reject non-authorized sources.
4) Add a targeted EDR sweep for endpoints of users who clicked the link.
5) Prepare disclosure notes for leadership and Legal if broader compromise confirmed.

Owner notes:
Marcus Chen (assignee) to coordinate forensics with SOC, SRE, and Eng infra. Aisha Patel (reporter) handling escalation to Legal and HR for potential social-engineering impact on People Ops branding.
